name: Moonchild
notes: The LA trio — "the lane's softest, most horn-and-vocoder-coloured instrumental soul", carried with the entry's **Gate 1 caveat** (independent label, but a defining name for this sub-idiom and a consistent Billboard jazz/R&B charter). `confidence` is **low** because the research rates the entry medium-low and marks tempo, drum and harmonic detail as inference. The drums are stated as a mix position: "programmed, small and very quiet — a filtered kick on 1 and 3, brushed or sampled snare on 2&4 mixed well down, sparse swung 16th hats, and fingersnaps; **the drum layer is the quietest element in the mix**". So the velocity tiers are the lowest in this section, the kick anchors are 1 and 3, the hat fill density is 0.2 and non-continuous, and the percussion gain is cut 8 dB. Harmony is "extension-heavy and static — maj9, m11 and sus voicings over 2-to-4-bar loops, with slow inner-voice movement and no functional cadence; the harmonic colour comes from stacked woodwind and vocal layers, not from chord change", hence `maxChords` 2, a raised `susSubstitutionProb` and long durations. Melody is "whisper-soft soprano at very low volume and very low note-density, doubled by a woodwind line" — density 1–4 with a legato articulation and a woodwind counter at −12. Bass is "soft synth-sub or played electric bass on the root, long decay, minimal motion; no 808 slides", so it is `mirror_kick` and not a `bass808` block. The arrangement is unusual and is authored: "songs run 3:00–4:30 with **no dynamic climax** — the arrangement stays at one intensity level, which is itself the parameter", which is why `switchUpProb` and the fill settings are the flattest here. ⚠ Every drum, melody and bass number is INFERRED. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“soft synth-sub or played electric bass on the root, long decay, minimal motion; no 808 slides.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 956/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.28 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. Second, `melody.densityPerBar` went from [1, 4] to [2, 5]. A lead allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves the counter almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter density recovers what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present rather than busier — the floor is what moved and the ceiling carries the density claim. ⚠ Every value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "the palette is the identity — Rhodes/Wurlitzer plus flute, alto sax, clarinet and bass clarinet stacked into pads, and vocoder/talkbox as a harmony instrument. All three members play multiple horns and keys. Melody is whisper-soft soprano at very low volume and very low note-density, doubled by a woodwind line.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
